LESSON: MANAGEMENT AND CONSERVATION OF THE ENVIRONMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environment
Topic 4.4: Management and Conservation of the Environment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Management and Conservation of the Environment, part of Natural and Historic Built Environment in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to conserve degraded environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. explore factors that lead to degradation of the environment in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the effects of environmental degradation in society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. design measures to manage and conserve the environment for sustainability,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. apply creative thinking skills in managing and conserving the immediate environment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Management and Conservation of the Environment in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. acknowledge the importance of managing and conserving the environment. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Management and Conservation of the Environment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem-solving: Learners explore possible solutions and their pro and cons as they develop

communication messages on how to creatively manage and conserve the environment.

• Citizenship: Learners demonstrate tolerance, express and understand different viewpoints as they participate in

environmental conservation in the community.

Values:
• Responsibility: Learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they participate in environmental conservation activities in

the community.

• Integrity: Learners are committed to duty as they participate in environmental conservation activities in the community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental education: Learners participate in environmental conservation in the community.

• Social cohesion: Learners work together in environmental conservation activities in the community.

Link to other learning areas:

• Learners use Integrated Science knowledge to research on factors that lead to degradation of the environment in the

community.

• Agriculture and Nutrition is relevant as learners view video clips or documentaries or pictures and write an essay on the

factors that leads degradation of the environment.
